title: Adapter shim for mixed-embedding deployments and phased retirement playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary: Introduce an adapter shim and operational playbook to safely onboard new embedding models alongside existing ones, support mixed-model serving for a period of coexistence, and provide a time-bounded, observable deprecation flow. This ticket covers the adapter implementation, compatibility checks, telemetry and eval gating, automated cohort rollouts, and runbook for deprecation notices and tenant migrations.

Background: We repeatedly see small quality deltas and unexpected downstream ranking regressions when swapping embedding models (customer search relevance, semantic retrieval). Full immediate swaps are high-risk for customers using vector stores with subtle differences in geometry (norms, scale). Several previous tickets recommended staged rollouts and contract checks but lacked an operational adapter that allows simultaneous serving and fine-grained traffic fencing.

Goal: Ship an adapter layer that: (1) accepts requests and routes them to a chosen model variant (primary, fallback, or dual-evaluate), (2) exposes per-tenant pinning and temporary shard routing, (3) collects unified telemetry for direct comparison, and (4) supports a documented phased retirement procedure for old models.

Scope: Adapter service code (+ SDK bindings), compatibility verifier for vector shape/precision/signature, a small cohort-routing controller in the API Gateway, dashboards and alert rules, an automated rollback trigger, and operator-facing runbook. Does NOT include persistent index migration tooling (handled in a follow-up).

Out-of-scope: On-prem packaging changes, customer-facing migration CLI (separate project), and any vector-store internal re-indexing automation.

Success metrics (first 2 months after release):
- No customer-facing incident attributed to embedding swap regressions.
- Average recall on our canonical eval set within 1.5% of baseline during each rollout stage.
- 95th percentile embed-generation latency increase <= 10ms for tenant traffic not in dual-evaluate mode.
- Runbook completeness verified with 2 SRE tabletop drills.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter accepts model alias and mode (primary, fallback, dual-evaluate) and routes correctly
SDK option to pin tenant to alias exposed and tested
Telemetry dashboard shows side-by-side recall/latency/error-rate for both models
Automated rollback triggers when gating SLIs breach thresholds
Documentation + runbook published and reviewed by Product and SRE
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: RFC draft uploaded to Confluence (link below). Initial design reviewed by Applied ML and Infra; core team formed (Aisha, Liam, Priya, Marco).
2026-03-11: Implemented initial adapter routing skeleton and unit tests. Added model alias header propagation in the gateway proxy. PR: github.com/redwood/inference/pull/4021
2026-03-12: End-to-end dual-evaluate flow validated locally with synthetic vector-store. Telemetry counters wired to metrics ingestion. Load test plan ready.
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for adapter routing and alias resolution. 2) Integration tests: SDK pinning + gateway routing + metrics emission. 3) Synthetic cohort experiment: run dual-evaluate at 5k qps with mixed sequences and validate recall/latency deltas. 4) Staging rollout to 3 internal tenants for 48 hours with manual SRE observation before wider canary.
telemetry_queries: 95p_embed_latency: SELECT percentile_cont(0.95, latency_ms) FROM embed_requests WHERE model_alias IN ('old','new') AND timeframe = '5m' GROUP BY model_alias
embed_quality_recall: SELECT model_alias, avg(recall_at_10) FROM embed_eval_results WHERE eval_set = 'canonical-regression' AND window='24h' GROUP BY model_alias
error_rate_comparison: SELECT model_alias, sum(errors)/sum(requests) FROM embed_request_aggregates WHERE window='10m' GROUP BY model_alias
rollout_policy: Phased: validate -> canary -> staged ramp -> full swap -> soft-retire -> hard-retire. Each stage has gating rules tied to telemetry. Default cohort scheduler: 0%->1%->5%->25%->50%->100% over a minimum of 24h between steps with gate checks. Dual-evaluate mode can be enabled to run both models and compare embeddings server-side without affecting downstream retrieval for up to 14 days.
rollout_steps: Preflight: signature and shape verification (dimension, dtype, normalization behavior). Reject variants that fail contract checks.
Shadow/dual-evaluate: run new model in parallel; collect paired embeddings and compute recall/embedding-drift metrics on sentinel queries.
Canary (1%): route 1% of non-critical tenants to new model, monitor gating SLIs (latency, recall, error-rate) for 24h
Staged ramp: increment cohorts 5% -> 25% -> 50% with 24h minimum windows and automated gate evaluation
Full swap: upon gates passing at 50% for 48h, schedule full swap and set 'soft-retire' flag on old model
Soft-retire: keep old model as fallback for 14 days with telemetry and migration notices
Hard-retire: after 30 days of stability and no pinned tenants, remove old model from catalog and update changelog
fallback_policy: Automatic reroute: if new-model error-rate > 2x baseline OR recall drop > 3% absolute on canonical eval, trigger immediate 5-minute traffic shift back to fallback model for affected cohorts and page on-call. Operator can also manually pin a tenant to fallback via console or SDK.
load_testing: Run k6 scenario targeting adapter with 20k QPS sustained for 1h (50% small requests, 50% long sequences). Verify no >5% increase in 99th percentile latency and no OOMs in serving pods. Baseline job: github.com/redwood/inference/actions/runner/emb-load-238
postmortem_plan: If an incident occurs, capture: timeline, affected cohorts, telemetry before/during/after, rollback actions, decision rationale. Schedule a blameless postmortem within 72 hours and publish learnings to the embedding playbook page.
migration_considerations: Notify customers with tenant-level pins 14 days before hard-retire. Provide example SDK call to re-pin: client.pinEmbeddingModel(tenant_id, 'model_alias'). Provide suggested retraining/reindex notes for common vector stores (Annoy/HNSW/FAISS) — e.g., check index recall degradation on a 1k-sample set and re-index if recall loss > 5%.
notes: We intentionally keep index migration out of this ticket to reduce blast radius; recommend a follow-up project that automates re-index workflows per datastore.
SRE tabletop scheduled for 2026-03-20 to validate runbook and paging thresholds.
Product requested a customer-facing migration timeline and opt-in form; follow-up with PM (see ENG-82300).
